decisions.choice: This verse is 2:1 in the Hebrew text, 1:18 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text begins chapter 2 with the second vision, so that chapter 1 holds only the first. Many Bibles end chapter 1 with this vision, numbering 2:1-4 as 1:18-21, and then begin their chapter 2 with the man with the measuring line (Hebrew 2:5), so their 2:1-13 is 2:5-17 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates, and Zechariah is cited by the Hebrew numbers.

decisions.choice: the second vision: four horns, and four craftsmen who throw them down
decisions.reason: A horn is the strength of an animal, and in the Bible it stands for power, especially the power of kings and nations (Psalm 75:5-6, 11; 1 Kings 22:11; Daniel 8:20-22). The angel explains that the horns are the powers that scattered God's people (verse 2), and the craftsmen are sent to throw them down (verse 4). The angel does not name the nations. Four is the number of the four directions (2:10; 6:5), so the horns may stand for every power, from every side, that had attacked Judah.

decisions.choice: I lifted up my eyes and saw: I looked up and saw something new
decisions.reason: The phrase marks the start of a new scene in a vision (2:5; 5:1; 6:1), as it does in stories (Genesis 18:2; 22:13).

decisions.choice: I looked up (B, R); look (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "looked up" for the idiom, and leave out "look", which only points to what was seen. The horns keep their name at every level, as set for Zechariah's visions.

decisions.choice: "alcé mis ojos y miré, y he aquí" (L); "levanté la vista y vi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The vision formula follows the term sheet: L keeps the Hebrew "look", B and R say "vi".

decisions.choice: "pembe" (horns), kept as the image at every level
decisions.reason: The horns stand for the nations' power; the image is kept at every level, as the term sheet says for the night visions, and the angel's explanation is translated, not expanded.

decisions.choice: "sừng" kept at every level
decisions.reason: The vision keeps its images (English terms note); the angel's explanation in verse 2 says what the horns are.

decisions.choice: "I lifted up my eyes and saw" is "눈을 들어 보니" (L, B) and "고개를 들어 보니" (R), here and in 2:5
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom is natural Korean too; Readable uses the everyday gesture. The Hebrew numbering (2:1 = 1:18 in many Bibles) is footnoted in the shared meaning decision.

ko.B: 내가 나와 말하던 천사에게 이것들이 무엇이냐고 물었다. 그가 대답했다. "이것들은 유다와 이스라엘과 예루살렘을 흩어 버린 뿔들이다."
ko.R: 내가 나와 말하던 천사에게 이것들이 무엇이냐고 물었다. 그가 말했다. "이것들은 유다와 이스라엘과 예루살렘을 흩어 버린 뿔들이다."

decisions.choice: scattered: drove the people into exile
decisions.reason: The verb is used for winnowing grain, tossing it so that the wind carries off the chaff (Isaiah 30:24), and for the scattering of the people among the nations (Jeremiah 31:10; Ezekiel 5:10). The horns are the powers that sent God's people into exile.

decisions.choice: Judah, Israel and Jerusalem: the whole people of God
alternatives: Israel as the northern kingdom, scattered by Assyria
decisions.reason: Israel may be the northern kingdom, which Assyria took into exile (2 Kings 17:6), named beside Judah and its capital, which Babylon destroyed. It may also be the name of the whole people. Either way, the three names cover all of God's people who were scattered. Verse 4 names Judah alone.

decisions.choice: These are the horns ... (every level)
decisions.reason: As set for Zechariah's visions, the angel's explanation is translated as he gives it, and no level adds who the horns are.

decisions.choice: the angel is "người" in the narrative, with no deity span
decisions.reason: The terms note: the angels of Zechariah take no deity span; "người" is the respectful third person used for him.

decisions.choice: craftsmen: skilled workers in wood, stone or metal
decisions.reason: The word is used for craftsmen of every kind (Exodus 35:35; Isaiah 44:12-13). Here they are probably workers with tools of iron, smiths who could cut or break off horns, though the text does not say what kind.

decisions.choice: the LORD himself showed me
decisions.reason: In most of the visions Zechariah simply sees, or the angel shows him. Here the LORD is the one who shows him, as he does in 3:1 (and compare Amos 7:1, 4, 7). The vision comes from God, not from Zechariah's own mind.

decisions.choice: skilled workers (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "skilled workers", a common phrase for people who work with their hands at a trade. The image is kept.

decisions.choice: "artesanos" (L, B); "trabajadores hábiles" (R)
decisions.reason: Harash is a skilled worker in wood, stone or metal; "artesanos" says that, and R uses plainer words, as the English R does.

decisions.choice: *charash* is "대장장이" (L, B) and "솜씨 좋은 일꾼" (R)
decisions.reason: The word covers workers in wood, stone and metal; men who strike down horns are pictured best as smiths, while Readable keeps the general sense as the English does.

records.literal_gloss: And I said, What [are] these coming to do? And he said, saying, These [are] the horns which scattered Judah, according to [the] mouth of [a] man not he lifted his head; and have come these to terrify them, to cast down [the] horns of the nations who lift a horn against [the] land of Judah to scatter it.

en.L: And I said, "What are these coming to do?" And he said, "These [are] the horns that scattered Judah, so that no one lifted up {{gender:their|his}} head; and these have come to terrify them, to throw down the horns of the nations that lifted up a horn against the land of Judah to scatter it."
en.B: I asked, "What are these coming to do?" He said, "Those are the horns that scattered Judah so completely that no one could raise {{gender:their|his}} head. But these craftsmen have come to terrify them, to throw down the horns of the nations that raised their horns against the land of Judah to scatter its people."
en.R: I asked, "What are these workers coming to do?" He said, "Those horns scattered the people of Judah so badly that no one could even lift {{gender:their|his}} head. These workers have come to terrify them and knock down the horns of the nations. Those nations raised their horns against the land of Judah to scatter its people."

fr.L: Et je dis : « Que viennent faire ceux-ci ? » Et il dit : « Ce [sont] les cornes qui ont dispersé Juda, au point que personne n’a levé la tête ; et ceux-ci sont venus pour les terrifier, pour abattre les cornes des nations qui ont levé la corne contre le pays de Juda pour le disperser. »
fr.B: Je demandai : « Que viennent faire ceux-là ? » Il dit : « Celles-là sont les cornes qui ont dispersé Juda, si bien que personne ne pouvait plus lever la tête. Mais ces artisans sont venus pour les terrifier, pour abattre les cornes des nations qui ont levé leurs cornes contre le pays de Juda pour en disperser les habitants. »
fr.R: J’ai demandé : « Que viennent faire ces ouvriers ? » Il a répondu : « Ces cornes ont tellement dispersé les gens de Juda que personne ne pouvait même plus lever la tête. Ces ouvriers sont venus pour les terrifier et abattre les cornes des nations. Ces nations ont levé leurs cornes contre le pays de Juda pour en disperser les habitants. »

es.L: Y dije: «¿Qué vienen a hacer estos?». Y él habló, diciendo: «Estos [son] los cuernos que dispersaron a Judá, de modo que nadie levantó la cabeza; y estos han venido para aterrorizarlos, para derribar los cuernos de las naciones que alzaron [el] cuerno contra la tierra de Judá para dispersarla».
es.B: Pregunté: «¿Qué vienen a hacer estos?». Él dijo: «Aquellos son los cuernos que dispersaron a Judá de tal manera que nadie podía levantar la cabeza. Pero estos artesanos han venido para aterrorizarlos, para derribar los cuernos de las naciones que alzaron sus cuernos contra la tierra de Judá para dispersar a su gente».
es.R: Pregunté: «¿Qué vienen a hacer estos trabajadores?». Él dijo: «Aquellos cuernos dispersaron a la gente de Judá tanto que nadie podía siquiera levantar la cabeza. Estos trabajadores han venido para aterrorizarlos y derribar los cuernos de las naciones. Esas naciones alzaron sus cuernos contra la tierra de Judá para dispersar a su gente».

sw.L: Nami nikasema, "Hawa wanakuja kufanya nini?" Naye akasema, "Hizi [ni] pembe zilizomtawanya Yuda, hata hakuna mtu aliyeinua kichwa chake; na hawa wamekuja kuzitia hofu, kuzitupa chini pembe za mataifa yaliyoinua pembe dhidi ya nchi ya Yuda ili kuitawanya."
sw.B: Nikauliza, "Hawa wanakuja kufanya nini?" Akasema, "Zile ni pembe zilizowatawanya Yuda kabisa hata hakuna mtu aliyeweza kuinua kichwa chake. Lakini mafundi hawa wamekuja kuzitia hofu, kuzitupa chini pembe za mataifa yaliyoinua pembe zao dhidi ya nchi ya Yuda ili kuwatawanya watu wake."
sw.R: Nikauliza, "Mafundi hawa wanakuja kufanya nini?" Akasema, "Zile pembe ziliwatawanya watu wa Yuda vibaya sana hata hakuna mtu aliyeweza kuinua kichwa chake. Mafundi hawa wamekuja kuzitia hofu na kuziangusha pembe za mataifa. Mataifa hayo yaliinua pembe zao dhidi ya nchi ya Yuda ili kuwatawanya watu wake."

vi.L: Tôi nói: "Những người này đến để làm gì?" Người đáp: "Đó [là] những cái sừng đã làm tan lạc Giu-đa, đến nỗi không ai ngẩng đầu lên được; còn những người này đến để làm cho chúng kinh hãi, để quăng xuống sừng của các nước đã giơ sừng lên nghịch cùng xứ Giu-đa để làm tan lạc nó."
vi.B: Tôi hỏi: "Những người này đến để làm gì?" Người đáp: "Đó là những cái sừng đã làm Giu-đa tan lạc đến nỗi không ai ngẩng đầu lên nổi. Nhưng những người thợ này đến để làm cho chúng kinh hãi, để quật ngã sừng của các nước đã giơ sừng lên nghịch cùng xứ Giu-đa hầu làm cho dân xứ ấy tan lạc."
vi.R: Tôi hỏi: "Những người thợ này đến để làm gì?" Người đáp: "Những cái sừng kia đã làm cho dân Giu-đa tan lạc tệ hại đến nỗi không ai ngẩng đầu lên nổi. Những người thợ này đến để làm cho chúng kinh hãi và đánh gãy sừng của các nước. Các nước ấy đã giơ sừng lên nghịch cùng xứ Giu-đa để làm cho dân xứ ấy tan lạc."

ko.L: 내가 말했다. "이들은 무엇을 하러 옵니까?" 그가 말했다. "저것들은 유다를 흩어 버려서 아무도 머리를 들지 못하게 한 뿔들이다. 그런데 이들이 와서 그것들을 두렵게 하고, 유다 땅을 향하여 뿔을 들어 그 땅을 흩어 버린 민족들의 뿔들을 떨어뜨리려고 한다."
ko.B: 내가 물었다. "이들은 무엇을 하러 옵니까?" 그가 말했다. "저 뿔들은 유다를 철저히 흩어 버려서 아무도 머리를 들지 못하게 했다. 그러나 이 대장장이들이 와서 그것들을 두렵게 하고, 유다 땅을 향하여 뿔을 들어 그 백성을 흩어 버린 민족들의 뿔들을 꺾어 버릴 것이다."
ko.R: 내가 물었다. "이 일꾼들은 무엇을 하러 옵니까?" 그가 말했다. "저 뿔들이 유다 백성을 몹시 흩어 놓아서 아무도 고개조차 들 수 없었다. 이 일꾼들은 그 뿔들을 겁에 질리게 하고, 민족들의 뿔들을 꺾어 버리러 왔다. 그 민족들은 유다 땅을 향하여 뿔을 들고 그 백성을 흩어 버렸다."

decisions.choice: so that no one lifted up his head: so completely that everyone was crushed and humbled
decisions.reason: "According to the mouth of a man" means "in proportion to", here "to such a degree that". Not lifting the head is a picture of defeat and shame (Judges 8:28; Job 10:15). The scattering left no one able to stand up straight.

decisions.choice: lifted up a horn against: rose up in proud strength against
decisions.reason: To lift up the horn is to act with power, often with arrogance (Psalm 75:5-6). The nations that raised their horns against Judah will have their horns thrown down.

decisions.choice: to throw down: to cast down and destroy the horns
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to throw or cast (Lamentations 3:53, of stones). Here it is used of horns, so it may mean to knock them down or cut them off. Either way the power of the nations is broken.

decisions.choice: to terrify them: the craftsmen frighten the horns, that is, the nations they stand for
decisions.reason: The word "them" has no clear reference in the Hebrew. It most likely points to the horns or the nations behind them. The angel does not say who the craftsmen are; the vision says only that God has agents ready to break every power that harmed his people.

decisions.choice: these craftsmen (B); these workers (R); its people (B, R); the gender setting
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "these", and the reader needs to know that the craftsmen are meant. "Scatter it" means scattering the land's people, as Balanced and Readable say. "No one lifted his head" means men and women alike, so the pronoun takes the gender setting. Readable splits the long explanation into sentences but keeps the horns.

decisions.choice: "personne n'a levé la tête", no gender span where the English has {{gender:their|his}} head
decisions.reason: French "personne" is already inclusive and needs no possessive here, so it takes no setting (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: "nadie ... la cabeza", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "nadie levantó la cabeza" has no possessive to choose, so the English gender span has no Spanish counterpart.

decisions.choice: "hakuna mtu ... kichwa chake" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Mtu" and "chake" cover everyone, so the English gender span has no Swahili counterpart.

decisions.choice: "không ai ngẩng đầu lên", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "ai" covers both and needs no possessive with "đầu"; the English gender span has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: one angel tells the other to run to Zechariah, the young man
alternatives: the young man is the man with the measuring line
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he said to him". Most likely the second angel sends the angel who talked with Zechariah back to him with the message. "This young man" is most likely Zechariah himself, who must pass the word on; some take him to be the man with the measuring line, who needs to know that Jerusalem cannot be measured. The message is the same either way.

decisions.choice: open villages: settlements without walls
decisions.reason: The word means open country towns with no walls (Ezekiel 38:11; Esther 9:19). Jerusalem will be like them, not because it is weak but because it will be too full of people and flocks for any wall to hold.

decisions.choice: people and livestock: a city full of life and wealth
decisions.reason: Flocks and herds were a family's wealth. A city with many people and animals is a prosperous one. In Zechariah's day, Jerusalem had few people and its walls were in ruins (compare Nehemiah 1:3; 7:4).

decisions.choice: that young man (B, R); like villages without walls (B); like a village with no walls around it (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "that young man", since the speaker is pointing to someone else. They add "like", to make plain that Jerusalem will be like open villages, not turned into them. The message to be passed on is in single quotation marks and closes at the end of verse 9.

decisions.choice: a wall of fire all around: the LORD himself will protect the city
decisions.reason: The city does not need walls of stone, for the LORD will surround it. The fire recalls the pillar of fire that guarded Israel in the wilderness (Exodus 13:21-22; 14:24) and Isaiah's promise of a glow of fire over Zion (Isaiah 4:5).

decisions.choice: I will be the glory in her midst: the LORD's own presence will return to the city
decisions.reason: Ezekiel saw the glory of the LORD leave the temple and the city before the fall of Jerusalem (Ezekiel 10:18-19; 11:23), and later saw it come back (Ezekiel 43:2-5). Haggai promised that the LORD would fill the new temple with glory (Haggai 2:7, 9). The LORD will not only guard the city from outside; he will live in it.

decisions.choice: I myself: the LORD stresses that he will do it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins with the pronoun "I", which it does not need, to stress who will be the city's wall.

decisions.choice: 2:10-17: a poem that calls the exiles home and promises the LORD's coming
decisions.reason: After the vision, the prophet speaks in verse: a call to the exiles still in Babylon to flee (verses 10-11), a word against the nations (verses 12-13) and a call to Zion to rejoice because the LORD is coming to live among his people (verses 14-17). The prophet speaks the LORD's words and, in verses 12-15, also of his own sending. As in the other prophets, the poem takes no quotation marks. It is set in lines.

decisions.choice: Ho! Ho!: an urgent call to listen and act
decisions.reason: The word is most often a cry of woe over those facing judgment (Isaiah 5:8), but it is also used to call out to people, as in Isaiah 55:1 ("Ho, everyone who thirsts"). Here it is doubled and followed by "flee", so it is a summons to hurry, not a threat.

decisions.choice: the land of the north: Babylon
decisions.reason: Verse 11 names Babylon. It lay to the east, but armies and travelers from there came into Judah from the north, so the prophets speak of the enemy as coming from the north (Jeremiah 1:14; 6:22). After Cyrus allowed the Jews to return in 538 BC, many stayed in Babylon; the poem calls them to come home.

decisions.choice: like the four winds I have spread you: I scattered you in every direction
alternatives: I will spread you out as widely as the four winds
I will gather you from the four winds
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for a completed act and usually means to spread out. Read with "flee", it looks back on the exile, when the LORD scattered his people to every quarter, as the wind blows in all directions (Ezekiel 17:21). Some read it as a promise that the LORD will make his people spread out widely in the future. The Greek translation reads "I will gather you from the four winds of heaven", which is a different sense and probably a smoothing of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: Ho! Ho! (L); Come! Come! (B); Hurry! Hurry! (R); no quotation marks; set in lines
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "Ho", as Isaiah 55:1 does for the same call. Balanced and Readable use a word that a reader hears as a summons, since this is not a cry of woe (m2). The lines follow the main division of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: *hoy* as a summons: "Ho !" (L), "Venez !" (B), "Vite !" (R), with no quotation marks
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for *hoy* when it calls people, not when it laments; the oracle is unquoted, as the English.

decisions.choice: "¡Eh!" (L), "¡Vengan!" (B), "¡Rápido!" (R)
decisions.reason: Hoy here is a summons, not a woe; the term sheet sets these words (uncertain). The verse is set in lines and takes no quotation marks, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Haya! Haya!" (L); "Njooni! Njooni!" (B); "Harakisheni! Harakisheni!" (R)
decisions.reason: Hoy here is a summons, not a woe, as the English of the Twelve settles ("Ho / Come / Hurry"); "Haya!" is the Swahili call to get moving, so it is not "Ole". The poem is set in lines, with no quotation marks, as the English.

decisions.choice: "Này!" (L) / "Hãy đến!" (B) / "Mau lên!" (R) for hoy as a summons
decisions.reason: The English terms note: here hoy is a summons, not a woe, so "Khốn cho" is not used; the poem takes no quotation marks and is set in lines as the English.

decisions.choice: *hoy* as a summons is "자," (L) and "어서" (B, R), here and in 2:11; the poem 2:10–17 takes no quotation marks and is set in lines
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording: here *hoy* calls the exiles home rather than pronouncing a woe. The land of the north is Babylon, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: Zion: the exiles of Jerusalem still living in Babylon
decisions.reason: Zion is the hill of Jerusalem and so the city and its people. Here it is the part of the people still in exile, called to escape as Isaiah and Jeremiah had called them (Isaiah 48:20; Jeremiah 51:6, 45).

decisions.choice: daughter of Babylon: Babylon pictured as a woman
decisions.reason: Cities are often pictured as women (Isaiah 47:1; Psalm 137:8). "Daughter of Babylon" means Babylon itself, not a daughter of it.

en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says. For the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent me against the nations that robbed you. \q Anyone who touches you touches the pupil of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eye.

es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto, por causa de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me ha enviado contra las naciones que {{plural_you:los|os}} saquearon: \q el que {{plural_you:los|os}} toca a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} toca la niña de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ojo.

vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán. Vì vinh quang của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã sai tôi đi nghịch cùng các nước đã cướp bóc các ngươi. \q Ai đụng đến các ngươi là đụng đến con ngươi mắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 영광 뒤에 그분께서 너희를 약탈한 민족들에게 나를 보내셨다. \q 너희를 건드리는 자는 그분의 눈동자를 건드리는 것이다.
ko.B: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 그분께서 그분의 영광을 위하여 너희를 약탈한 민족들에게 나를 보내셨다. \q 너희를 건드리는 자는 그분의 눈동자를 건드리는 것이다.
ko.R: 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 그분께서 그분의 영광을 위하여 너희를 약탈한 민족들에게 나를 보내셨다. \q 너희를 건드리는 사람은 그분의 눈동자를 건드리는 것이다.

decisions.choice: after glory: for the sake of the LORD's glory
alternatives: after the glory appeared, he sent me
decisions.reason: These two words are among the hardest in the book. "After" can mean "behind" or "for the sake of", and "glory" can mean God's glory or honor in general. Read one way, the LORD sent the speaker to the nations for his glory: to win honor for the LORD by bringing judgment. Read another way, the speaker was sent after the glory had been revealed, perhaps the glory promised in verse 9. The translation takes the first; the sense of the verse, that the LORD will act against the nations, is the same.

decisions.choice: sent me: the prophet, sent with this message
alternatives: a figure sent by the LORD
decisions.reason: The speaker says that the LORD of hosts has sent him, and three times adds that when the promise comes true, "you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me" (verses 13, 15; 4:9; 6:15). This is the test of a true prophet (Deuteronomy 18:21-22), so the speaker is most likely Zechariah. Some read him as the angel, or as a messenger of the LORD whom later readers saw as the Messiah.

decisions.choice: the pupil of his eye: what is most precious and most easily hurt
decisions.reason: The eye is guarded by instinct against the smallest touch. To touch God's people is to strike at what God holds most dear and guards most closely (Deuteronomy 32:10; Psalm 17:8).

decisions.choice: his eye: the LORD's eye
decisions.reason: The word for pupil is found only here. Jewish scribal tradition lists this verse among a few places where the scribes changed "my" to "his" out of reverence, so that the text would not speak of touching God's own eye; the original then said "my eye". The Hebrew as it stands can also be read of the attacker's own eye: whoever harms Israel harms himself. The translation reads it of the LORD, as Deuteronomy 32:10 does. This description of the scribal tradition is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: the pupil of his eye (all levels); after glory (L); for the sake of his glory (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Pupil of his eye" is the wording of Deuteronomy 32:10 at each level. "Apple of the eye", an old English idiom, now means a favorite, which is weaker than the picture. Literal keeps "after glory" and leaves its sense open; Balanced and Readable give the sense chosen in m1. "Plundered" (L, B) becomes "robbed" at Readable.

decisions.choice: "la niña de su ojo"
decisions.reason: The pupil of the eye is "la niña del ojo" in Spanish, the same picture as the Hebrew; deity_pronoun follows the English on "su".

decisions.choice: "mboni ya jicho lake"
decisions.reason: The pupil of the eye is "mboni ya jicho", the most precious and tender part; the possessive refers to God and takes the span. "Me" is the messenger and takes none.

decisions.choice: the messenger sent says "tôi"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: "me" is the prophet sent with the message; he speaks as "tôi", and "he" (the LORD) takes the deity span.

decisions.choice: "con ngươi mắt" for the pupil of the eye
decisions.reason: The usual Vietnamese idiom for what is most precious and most easily hurt, at every level as the English keeps it.

decisions.choice: The messenger who is sent speaks of the LORD with -시- and "그분" ("그분께서 … 나를 보내셨다", "그분의 눈동자"); where the LORD speaks in the first person (2:13a, 15a) there is no honorific
alternatives: the same form for both voices
decisions.reason: As the meaning decisions say, the voice moves between the LORD and his messenger; Korean marks the turn by the honorific, which the English shows only with the deity spans.

source.text: כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֨י מֵנִ֤יף אֶת־יָדִי֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔םוְהָי֥וּ שָׁלָ֖ל לְעַבְדֵיהֶ֑ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּֽי־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁלָחָֽנִי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For look, I [am] about to wave my hand over them, and they will be plunder for their slaves; and you will know that Yahweh of hosts has sent me.

en.L: For look, I am about to wave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand over them, and they will be plunder for their own slaves; \q and you shall know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has sent me.
en.B: I am about to raise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against them, and they will be plundered by their own slaves. \q Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me.
en.R: I am going to raise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to strike them, and they will be robbed by the people they made their slaves. \q Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me.

fr.L: Car voici, je vais agiter {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main sur elles, et elles deviendront un butin pour leurs propres esclaves ; \q et vous saurez que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé.
fr.B: Je vais lever {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main contre elles, et elles seront pillées par leurs propres esclaves. \q Alors vous saurez que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé.
fr.R: Je vais lever {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main pour les frapper, et elles seront dépouillées par ceux qu’elles avaient réduits en esclavage. \q Alors vous saurez que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé.

es.L: Porque he aquí, yo agito {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano sobre ellos, y serán botín para sus propios esclavos; \q y {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos me ha enviado.
es.B: Voy a levantar {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano contra ellos, y serán saqueados por sus propios esclavos. \q Entonces {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos me ha enviado.
es.R: Voy a levantar {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano para castigarlos, y los saquearán las personas que ellos hicieron esclavas. \q Entonces {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos me ha enviado.

sw.L: Kwa maana tazama, ninakaribia kuutikisa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} juu yao, nao watakuwa nyara kwa watumwa wao wenyewe; \q nanyi mtajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma.
sw.B: Ninakaribia kuuinua mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} dhidi yao, nao watatekwa nyara na watumwa wao wenyewe. \q Ndipo mtajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma.
sw.R: Ninakwenda kuuinua mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kuwapiga, nao watanyang'anywa mali na watu waliowafanya watumwa wao. \q Ndipo mtajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma.

vi.L: Vì kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sắp vung tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trên chúng, và chúng sẽ thành của cướp cho chính nô lệ của chúng; \q và các ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi.
vi.B: Ta sắp giơ tay nghịch cùng chúng, và chúng sẽ bị chính nô lệ của mình cướp bóc. \q Bấy giờ các ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi.
vi.R: Ta sắp giơ tay đánh chúng, và chúng sẽ bị cướp bóc bởi chính những người chúng đã bắt làm nô lệ. \q Bấy giờ các ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi.

ko.L: 보라, 내가 그들 위에 내 손을 휘두르겠다. 그러면 그들이 자기들의 종들에게 약탈물이 될 것이다. \q 그때에 너희는 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 보내신 줄 알 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 손을 들어 그들을 치면, 그들은 자기들의 종들에게 약탈을 당할 것이다. \q 그때에 너희는 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 손을 들어 그들을 치겠다. 그러면 그들은 자기들이 종으로 부리던 사람들에게 빼앗길 것이다. \q 그때에 너희는 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.

decisions.choice: wave my hand over them: raise the hand to strike
decisions.reason: To wave or shake the hand over someone is a threatening gesture before a blow (Isaiah 11:15; 19:16). Here the LORD is the one who raises his hand against the nations.

decisions.choice: my hand ... sent me: the LORD speaks, and then his messenger
decisions.reason: "My hand" is the LORD's, but "the LORD of hosts has sent me" is said by the messenger. The prophet passes from speaking the LORD's words to speaking about his own task without a break, as prophets often do.

decisions.choice: plunder for their own slaves: the nations' power will be turned upside down
decisions.reason: The nations that plundered God's people (verse 12) will be plundered by those they had made their slaves. The reversal is like Isaiah 14:2.

decisions.choice: slaves, at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "slave" at every level where slavery itself is the point. Here the masters are plundered by the people they had enslaved, and "servants" would hide the reversal.

decisions.choice: "esclavos" at every level
decisions.reason: Here the point is the reversal of slavery itself, so "esclavos" is kept at every level, as the English keeps "slaves".

decisions.choice: "watumwa" at every level
decisions.reason: Slavery itself is the point here, so "mtumwa" is used at every level, as the style guide sets.

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" at every level
decisions.reason: Here the word is slavery itself, so the Isaiah note keeps "nô lệ" (God's servants are "đầy tớ").

decisions.choice: "slaves" is "종" at every level
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "종" for *'eved*; the English "slaves" is one word at every level, and so is the Korean.

source.text: רָנִּ֥י וְשִׂמְחִ֖י בַּת־צִיּ֑וֹן כִּ֧י הִנְנִי־בָ֛א וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Shout for joy and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for look, I [am] coming and I will dwell in your midst, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: Shout for joy and rejoice, daughter of Zion, \q for look, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Sing and rejoice, Daughter Zion, \q for I am coming to live among you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: People of Zion, sing and be glad! \q I am coming, and I will live among you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

fr.L: Pousse des cris de joie et réjouis-toi, fille de Sion, \q car voici, je viens, et j’habiterai au milieu de toi, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Chante et réjouis-toi, fille de Sion, \q car je viens habiter au milieu de toi, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Peuple de Sion, chante et sois heureux ! \q Je viens, et j’habiterai au milieu de toi, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

es.L: Grita de júbilo y alégrate, hija de Sion, \q porque he aquí, yo vengo, y habitaré en medio de ti, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Canta y alégrate, hija de Sion, \q porque vengo a vivir en medio de ti, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: ¡Pueblo de Sion, canta y alégrate! \q Yo vengo, y viviré en medio de ti, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Piga kelele kwa furaha na ushangilie, binti Sayuni, \q kwa maana tazama, ninakuja, nami nitakaa katikati yako, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Imba na ufurahi, Binti Sayuni, \q kwa maana ninakuja kukaa kati yako, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Enyi watu wa Sayuni, imbeni na kufurahi! \q Ninakuja, nami nitaishi kati yenu, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Hãy reo vui và vui mừng, hỡi con gái Si-ôn, \q vì kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang đến, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ngự giữa ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Hãy ca hát và vui mừng, hỡi con gái Si-ôn, \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang đến để ngự giữa con, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Hỡi dân Si-ôn, hãy ca hát và vui mừng! \q Ta đang đến, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ở giữa con, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 딸 시온아, 기뻐 외치며 즐거워하여라. \q 보라, 내가 가서 네 가운데 머물겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 딸 시온아, 노래하며 기뻐하여라. \q 내가 너희 가운데 살려고 간다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 시온 백성아, 노래하며 기뻐하여라! \q 내가 가서 너희 가운데 살겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: I am coming and I will dwell in your midst: the LORD's own presence among his people
decisions.reason: The verb "dwell" is the one used for the LORD's living among Israel in the tabernacle (Exodus 25:8; 29:45-46). Ezekiel had promised that he would live among his people forever (Ezekiel 43:7, 9). The promise returns in 8:3.

decisions.choice: shout for joy and rejoice, daughter of Zion
decisions.reason: Zephaniah 3:14-15 calls Zion to sing and rejoice because the LORD is in her midst, and Zechariah 9:9 repeats the call when Zion's king comes. On "daughter of Zion", see the note at Isaiah 1:8.

decisions.choice: daughter of Zion (L); Daughter Zion (B); people of Zion (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording from Isaiah. Balanced and Readable leave out "look", and Readable says "live among you" for "dwell in your midst".

decisions.choice: "hija de Sion" (L, B); "pueblo de Sion" (R)
decisions.reason: Daughter Zion follows the Spanish of Isaiah at each level, with feminine "tú".

decisions.choice: "binti Sayuni" (L); "Binti Sayuni" (B); "watu wa Sayuni" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Isaiah block and Zephaniah 3:14.

decisions.choice: God speaks to daughter Zion as "con" (B, R), "ngươi" (L)
decisions.reason: The Isaiah note: God says "ngươi" (L) / "con" (B, R) to Zion in promises.

source.text: וְנִלְווּ֩ גוֹיִ֨ם רַבִּ֤ים אֶל־יְהוָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְהָ֥יוּ לִ֖י לְעָ֑ם וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֣י בְתוֹכֵ֔ךְ וְיָדַ֕עַתְּ כִּי־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֵלָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will join themselves many nations to Yahweh in that day, and they will become for me a people; and I will dwell in your midst, and you will know that Yahweh of hosts has sent me to you.

en.L: And many nations will join themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in that day, and they will be a people for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q and I will dwell in your midst, and you shall know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has sent me to you.
en.B: Many nations will join themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on that day and will become {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q I will live among you, and you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me to you.
en.R: At that time many nations will join themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and become {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q I will live among you. Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me to you.

fr.L: Et beaucoup de nations s’attacheront {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} en ce jour-là, et elles seront pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} un peuple ; \q et j’habiterai au milieu de toi, et tu sauras que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé vers toi.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, de nombreuses nations s’attacheront {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et deviendront {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple. \q J’habiterai au milieu de toi, et tu sauras que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé vers toi.
fr.R: En ce temps-là, beaucoup de nations s’uniront {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et deviendront {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple. \q J’habiterai au milieu de toi. Alors tu sauras que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées m’a envoyé vers toi.

es.L: Y se unirán muchas naciones {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} en aquel día, y serán para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} un pueblo; \q y habitaré en medio de ti, y sabrás que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos me ha enviado a ti.
es.B: Aquel día muchas naciones se unirán {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y llegarán a ser {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo. \q Viviré en medio de ti, y sabrás que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos me ha enviado a ti.
es.R: En ese tiempo muchas naciones se unirán {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y serán {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo. \q Viviré en medio de ti. Entonces sabrás que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos me ha enviado a ti.

sw.L: Na mataifa mengi yataungana na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} katika siku ile, nayo yatakuwa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}; \q nami nitakaa katikati yako, nawe utajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma kwako.
sw.B: Mataifa mengi yataungana na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} siku hiyo na kuwa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. \q Nitakaa kati yako, nawe utajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma kwako.
sw.R: Wakati huo mataifa mengi yataungana na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kuwa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. \q Nitaishi kati yenu. Ndipo mtajua kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amenituma kwenu.

vi.L: Trong ngày ấy nhiều nước sẽ gắn bó với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và họ sẽ làm dân của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ngự giữa ngươi, và ngươi sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi đến cùng ngươi.
vi.B: Vào ngày ấy nhiều nước sẽ gắn bó với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và trở thành dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Ta sẽ ngự giữa con, và con sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi đến với con.
vi.R: Vào lúc ấy nhiều nước sẽ gắn bó với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và trở thành dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Ta sẽ ở giữa con. Bấy giờ con sẽ biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã sai tôi đến với con.

ko.L: 그날에 많은 민족들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게 연합하여 나의 백성이 될 것이다. \q 내가 네 가운데 머물 것이니, 너는 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너에게 보내신 줄 알 것이다.
ko.B: 그날에 많은 민족이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게 와서 연합하고, 내 백성이 될 것이다. \q 내가 너희 가운데 살 것이다. 그러면 너희는 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너희에게 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 그때에 많은 민족이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게 와서 하나가 되어 내 백성이 될 것이다. \q 내가 너희 가운데 살 것이다. 그러면 너희는 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 너희에게 보내신 줄 알게 될 것이다.

decisions.choice: many nations will join themselves to the LORD and become his people
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of foreigners who "join themselves to the LORD" in Isaiah 56:3, 6. The words "they will be my people" are the words of God's covenant with Israel (Jeremiah 31:33; Zechariah 8:8); here they include the nations. The same hope closes the book's first half (8:20-23).

decisions.choice: for me ... has sent me: the LORD speaks, then the messenger
decisions.reason: As in verse 13, "me" first refers to the LORD and then to the one he has sent. "You" is feminine singular: Zion is addressed.

decisions.choice: in that day (L); on that day (B); at that time (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase in the prophets.

decisions.choice: "toi", "tu sauras" in verses 14-15 for daughter Zion
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" here is feminine singular, Zion addressed as a woman, so French keeps "tu" where English cannot show the number.

decisions.choice: singular "sabrás", "a ti"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" here is feminine singular, Zion, so Spanish uses "tú" and no plural_you span.

decisions.choice: "trong ngày ấy" (L) / "vào ngày ấy" (B) / "vào lúc ấy" (R)
decisions.reason: The Isaiah terms note's wording for "in that day".

source.text: וְנָחַ֨ל יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יְהוּדָה֙ חֶלְק֔וֹ עַ֖ל אַדְמַ֣ת הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ וּבָחַ֥ר ע֖וֹד בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will inherit Yahweh Judah [as] his portion on the land the holy, and he will choose again Jerusalem.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will inherit Judah [as] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} portion upon the holy land, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will again choose Jerusalem.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will possess Judah as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} share in the holy land, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will once again choose Jerusalem.
en.R: Judah will belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own share in the holy land. \q He will choose Jerusalem again.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} héritera Juda [comme] {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} part sur la terre sainte, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} choisira encore Jérusalem.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} possédera Juda comme {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} part dans la terre sainte, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} choisira de nouveau Jérusalem.
fr.R: Juda appartiendra {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} comme {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} part à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dans la terre sainte. \q Il choisira encore Jérusalem.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} heredará a Judá [como] {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} porción en la tierra santa, \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} escogerá otra vez a Jerusalén.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} poseerá a Judá como {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} parte en la tierra santa, \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} volverá a escoger a Jerusalén.
es.R: Judá le pertenecerá {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} como {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia parte en la tierra santa. \q Volverá a escoger a Jerusalén.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamrithi Yuda [kama] fungu {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} katika nchi takatifu, \q naye ataichagua Yerusalemu tena.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataimiliki Yuda kama fungu {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} katika nchi takatifu, \q naye ataichagua Yerusalemu tena.
sw.R: Yuda itakuwa mali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, fungu {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} katika nchi takatifu. \q Ataichagua Yerusalemu tena.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ nhận Giu-đa làm sản nghiệp, [làm] phần của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên đất thánh, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ lại chọn Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ nhận Giu-đa làm phần riêng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong đất thánh, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ lại chọn Giê-ru-sa-lem một lần nữa.
vi.R: Giu-đa sẽ thuộc về {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, là phần riêng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong đất thánh. \q Ngài sẽ lại chọn Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 거룩한 땅에서 유다를 그분의 몫으로 차지하시고, \q 다시 예루살렘을 택하실 것이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 거룩한 땅에서 유다를 그분의 몫으로 차지하시고, \q 다시 한번 예루살렘을 택하실 것이다.
ko.R: 유다는 거룩한 땅에서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 차지하실 몫이 될 것이다. \q 그분께서 다시 예루살렘을 택하실 것이다.

decisions.choice: inherit Judah as his portion: claim Judah as his own share
decisions.reason: The verb means to receive or hold as one's inheritance. Deuteronomy 32:9 says, "The LORD's portion is his people". Here the LORD claims Judah again as his own.

decisions.choice: the holy land: the land made holy by the LORD's presence
decisions.reason: This is the only place in the Bible where the land is called "the holy land". It is holy because the LORD will live there (verses 14-15).

decisions.choice: he will again choose Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The promise of 1:17 repeated; see the note there.

decisions.choice: Judah will belong to the LORD (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes Judah the subject, which says the same thing in plainer words.

source.text: הַ֥ס כָּל־בָּשָׂ֖ר מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֥י נֵע֖וֹר מִמְּע֥וֹן קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Hush, all flesh, before Yahweh, for he has roused himself from [the] dwelling of his holiness.

en.L: Hush, all flesh, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has roused {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy dwelling.
en.B: Be silent before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all people, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has risen up from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy dwelling.
en.R: Everyone, be silent before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q He has gotten up and come out from the holy place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives.

fr.L: Silence, toute chair, devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:s’|S’}}est réveillé de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sainte demeure.
fr.B: Faites silence devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, vous tous, les humains, \q car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:s’|S’}}est levé de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sainte demeure.
fr.R: Que tout le monde fasse silence devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! \q Il {{deity_pronoun:s’|S’}}est levé et il sort du lieu saint où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} habite.

es.L: ¡Silencio, toda carne, delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}!, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se ha levantado de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santa morada.
es.B: ¡Guarde silencio delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} toda la humanidad!, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se ha levantado de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santa morada.
es.R: ¡Que todo el mundo guarde silencio delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! \q Se ha levantado y ha salido del lugar santo donde {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} vive.

sw.L: Nyamazeni, wenye mwili wote, mbele ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q kwa maana ameamka kutoka makao {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} matakatifu.
sw.B: Nyamazeni mbele ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, enyi watu wote, \q kwa maana ameinuka kutoka makao {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} matakatifu.
sw.R: Kila mtu na anyamaze mbele ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Ameinuka, ametoka mahali patakatifu anapoishi.

vi.L: Hỡi mọi xác thịt, hãy im lặng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã trỗi dậy từ nơi ngự thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Hỡi mọi người, hãy lặng im trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đứng dậy từ nơi ngự thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Mọi người hãy im lặng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! \q Ngài đã đứng dậy và ra khỏi nơi thánh mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngự.

ko.L: 모든 육체여, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 잠잠하여라. \q 그분께서 그분의 거룩한 처소에서 일어나셨기 때문이다.
ko.B: 모든 사람아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 잠잠하여라. \q 그분께서 그분의 거룩한 처소에서 일어나셨다.
ko.R: 모든 사람아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 조용히 하여라! \q 그분께서 일어나 그분께서 계시는 거룩한 곳에서 나오셨다.

decisions.choice: be silent before the LORD: hushed awe before God who is about to act
decisions.reason: The same call is found in Habakkuk 2:20 and Zephaniah 1:7. Silence is the response of creatures when God comes to act.

decisions.choice: all flesh: all humankind
decisions.reason: "Flesh" stands for human beings in their weakness and mortality, as in Joel 3:1. Every person, in every nation, is to be still.

decisions.choice: he has roused himself from his holy dwelling: the LORD has risen to act
decisions.reason: The verb is used of waking up or stirring oneself to action (Psalm 44:24; Isaiah 51:9). The LORD's holy dwelling is heaven (Deuteronomy 26:15; Jeremiah 25:30). He is coming out to do what he has promised.

decisions.choice: all flesh (L); all people (B); everyone (R)
decisions.reason: As set for Joel 3:1, Literal keeps "all flesh", and the other levels say what it means. Readable says "gotten up and come out" for "roused himself", to make the picture plain.

decisions.choice: "toda carne" (L); "toda la humanidad" (B); "todo el mundo" (R)
decisions.reason: "All flesh" is kept at L, as the term sheet sets for Joel 3:1 L; B and R say who is meant. The call is in the third person, so it needs no plural_you span.

decisions.choice: "wenye mwili wote" (L); "enyi watu wote" (B); "Kila mtu" (R)
decisions.reason: "All flesh" means all humankind; Literal keeps "mwili", as Joel 3:1 "kila mwenye mwili".

decisions.choice: "hãy im lặng trước mặt CHÚA", as Habakkuk 2:20 and Zephaniah 1:7 in this job
decisions.reason: The allusion decision: the same call to silence; the Vietnamese keeps one wording.

decisions.choice: "all flesh" is "모든 육체" (L) and "모든 사람" (B, R); "hush" is "잠잠하여라" (L, B) and "조용히 하여라" (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet's Joel 3:1 (L 모든 육체, B, R 모든 사람) and the Korean Habakkuk 2:20 and Zephaniah 1:7.
